reviews.body: Found a production migration blocker, an unhandled conflict in the web client, and missing customer-route test coverage. Production contains 37 case-insensitive duplicate email groups across 74 customer rows; typechecking and all 9 existing tests pass.

comments.body:
🔴 **P0** · 🐛 **Bug**

This index cannot be created on production: a read-only check found **37 duplicate `lower(email)` groups covering 74 customer rows**, all with case variants. `db:migrate` will fail and roll back this migration. Add an explicit duplicate-resolution step that preserves customer/invoice relationships before building the index; lowercasing the existing emails alone will not remove the collisions.

Reproduce the check:
```sql
select count(*) as groups, coalesce(sum(n), 0) as rows
from (
  select lower(email), count(*) as n
  from public.customers
  group by lower(email)
  having count(*) > 1
) d;
```

🟠 **P1** · ⚠️ **Error handling**

Submitting an existing email through invoices-web now produces an uncaught server-action error. `invoices-web/lib/api.ts:78–81` throws `ApiError` for this 409, `app/customers/actions.ts:9–13` lets it escape, and `app/customers/new/page.tsx:9–23` has no form error state. The user gets an application error instead of an email-conflict message they can correct. Link and ship a companion web PR that catches status 409 and displays the conflict in the form before or alongside this API change.

🟡 **P2** · 🐛 **Bug**

The new tests only check SQLSTATE detection; neither changed customer route nor email normalization is covered. Add route tests for lower-case persistence on POST/PATCH, a case-insensitive duplicate returning the documented 409 body, updating a customer's email to its own case variant succeeding, and unrelated database errors still reaching the 500 handler. These exercise the new behavior rather than just its helper.
